transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Please have a seat. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Uh… yeah. I guess what brings me in is my eating’s gotten kind of out of hand, especially after late shifts. I’ll stop for takeout, and it’s not just a sandwich or something — it’ll be like two burgers, fries, a shake… and then I get home and I’m still poking around, finishing leftovers out in the garage like it’s some second dinner.

I don’t know, it sounds ridiculous saying it out loud. I work production, so sometimes I tell myself I’m just hungry from the shift, but… it’s more than that.
When you find yourself eating large amounts of food, especially after your shifts, do you feel like you can’t control it — like it’s hard to stop eating once you start?

Yeah… that’s pretty much it. Once I start, it’s like a switch gets flipped or something. I’ll be standing there with the bag open, and in my head I’m saying, Roy, shut the bag and go inside, you don’t need any more of this.

And then my hand just… keeps going back in. Like I’m watching myself do it.

It’s weird, because at work I can follow procedures all day — safety stuff, timing, all that — but with that food in front of me, after a shift, it’s like the sensible part of me gets shoved to the side.
After these episodes of eating, how do you feel about yourself? Do you feel guilty, ashamed, or upset with how much you ate?

Yeah… I do. I feel pretty lousy afterward. Ashamed, mostly. Kind of disgusted with myself, if I’m being honest.

It’s strange because I’ve always thought of myself as a pretty disciplined person — I mean, at work people count on me, I show up, I do what I’m supposed to do. My dad was like that too, big on being dependable, not making excuses… anyway.

So when I’m out there eating like that, or sneaking food like I don’t want anyone to see, afterward it just hits me like, what are you doing? It feels like I’m letting myself down.
After you eat like that, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I’m not sure I’d say I do that, exactly. I mean, afterward I definitely think, okay, tomorrow you’ve got to get yourself together, maybe skip the junk, that kind of thing.

But as far as… making myself sick or taking something, I don’t really know—no, that’s not what usually happens. The exercise thing, I mean, I’m on my feet a lot at work already, and my knees aren’t exactly what they used to be, so it’s not like I go run five miles or anything. Mostly I just feel bad and tell myself I’ll do better the next day.
Can you tell me more about those times when you're eating — do you ever feel like you can't stop, even if you want to, or like you're not really in control of what or how much you're eating?

Yeah, that’s… that’s exactly what it feels like. Like once I start, something sort of flips. I’ll be standing there telling myself, Roy, close the bag, go inside, you’re done, and then my hand just keeps reaching back in anyway.

It’s not like I’m thinking, Oh great, let’s keep doing this. I’m usually already mad at myself while it’s happening. But it’s like the stopping part doesn’t kick in. I don’t know… kind of like when a machine at work keeps cycling even after you know something’s off—sorry, that’s probably a weird comparison. But yeah, I don’t feel fully in control of it.
Have you ever tried to stop yourself from eating during one of these episodes, and if so, do you feel like you can’t actually stop until you’ve eaten a lot more than you intended?

Yeah… I’ve tried. Plenty of times. I’ll be right in the middle of it thinking, Roy, just shut the bag, put it down, go back inside… and I mean, I know what I’m supposed to do.

But it’s like once I’ve started, the switch is already flipped. My hands just keep going back for more even while I’m arguing with myself in my head. It’s embarrassing to say, because I’m not usually someone who—well, at work if something needs doing, I do it, you know? But with that, in the moment, I don’t feel like I can actually stop until I’ve gone way past what I meant to eat.
When you’re eating during these episodes, are you actually hungry, or does it feel like you’re eating even though you’re not really hungry?

I don’t know that I’ve really paid attention to that part, honestly. I mean, sometimes I tell myself I’m just getting a snack, but whether I’m actually hungry-hungry… I don’t always stop and check.

It’s funny, at work I can tell you exactly when I need lunch because my stomach’s growling and I’m watching the clock, but at home it’s more… I don’t know, automatic maybe? I’d have to think about it more. I’m not sure I could say for certain either way.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual, like you're rushing through it without really thinking about it?

Yeah… yeah, I do. Especially if I’m in my truck or out in the workshop. I’ll eat so fast that half the time I don’t even really taste it.

It’s almost like I’m trying to get it down before somebody comes around or notices, even if there’s nobody actually there. Which is stupid, I know. The workshop’s mine, mostly, and my truck is just—well, it’s not like I’m on a lunch break at the plant with guys walking by. But I’ll still rush through it like that, just kind of shoveling it in without really thinking.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full, even if you didn’t mean to eat that much?

Yeah… that happens. Not every—well, I guess enough that I notice it.

By the time I finally stop, my stomach’s so tight against my work pants that I’m sitting there leaned back, like I don’t even want to move for a while. It’s that kind of uncomfortable where you’re thinking, why did I keep going?

And those pants aren’t exactly forgiving, either. I’ve worn the same kind for years at the plant, and they’re stiff as cardboard when they come out of the wash. But yeah… I end up way fuller than I meant to be.
When you're having one of these episodes where you feel out of control with eating, does it happen within a short period of time — like over the course of just a couple hours?

Yeah, it’s usually not like an all-day grazing thing, if that’s what you mean. It’s more packed into a short stretch.

Like after a late shift, I’ll swing through for takeout — and I tell myself it’s dinner, you know, because I was working late — but then I’ll end up with two burgers, fries, a shake… and I’ll eat that pretty quick. Then I get home and somehow I’m out in the garage going through leftovers like it’s a second supper.

I mean, I can spend all day at the plant doing the same routine, clock in, clock out, everything measured down to the minute, and then after work it’s like the time gets fuzzy. But yeah, the actual eating part, that’s usually over a couple hours, not spread out forever.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you’re embarrassed about how much you’re eating?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I don’t really like admitting that, but yeah.

Like I’ll be at dinner with my wife and act like I’m not that hungry, just kind of pick at what’s there, say I had a big lunch or whatever. And then later, if she’s busy watching something or on the phone with her sister — her sister can talk forever, I swear — I’ll slip out to the truck or out by the garage and eat there.

It’s not even comfortable, eating in the truck like that. Stuff balanced on the seat, napkins everywhere. But I’d rather do that than have her see how much I’m actually putting away. It’s embarrassing. She wouldn’t be cruel about it, but… I don’t want that look, you know?
Do you find yourself really focused on your weight or the way your body looks, maybe to the point where it bothers you a lot or affects how you feel about yourself?

I don’t know… I mean, I notice it, sure. Hard not to when your clothes fit different or you catch yourself in the mirror getting ready for work.

But “really focused,” I’m not sure. I’m not standing there measuring myself or anything like that. Mostly I just get irritated, like when a shirt pulls weird or my belt’s on a different notch. Then I’ll think about it for a bit and go on with my day.

Although, those work uniforms, they make everybody look bad, honestly. Same gray pants, same stiff shirts — nobody’s winning a fashion contest at the plant. So I don’t know if it’s my body I’m thinking about or just feeling uncomfortable in general. I guess it bothers me some, but I’m not sure it’s the main thing.
Do you ever feel upset or worried about your body shape or weight when you're having these episodes of eating, like it’s influencing why you eat the way you do?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s like… driving it, exactly.

I mean, sometimes I’ll feel lousy about how my stomach feels or how my pants fit, but when I’m in one of those eating spells, I don’t think I’m sitting there thinking, “I hate how I look, so I’m going to eat.” It’s more like I’m just in it, and then afterward I’ll think, well, that didn’t help anything.

But I don’t know. Maybe it’s mixed in there somewhere. Like the other day at work they changed the lockers around, and I had to squeeze past this row of guys during shift change — everybody’s got lunch pails and boots and all that — and I remember feeling awkward about taking up space. Then later that night I ate too much. But whether those are connected, I couldn’t really tell you.
Do you usually feel a strong emotional urge or need to eat like this, especially when you're stressed, upset, or just feeling off?

Yeah… I think that’s closer to it, maybe. Not always like I’m crying or something, but there’s this urge that gets going.

Like once I start, it feels like somebody flipped a switch. I’ll even be saying in my head, “Roy, shut the bag and go back inside,” and then my hand’s already reaching in again. It’s stupid, because I know exactly what I’m doing, but I’m not really stopping.

Stress probably makes it worse. Work’s been a mess with the line changes — they move one thing and suddenly everybody’s acting like the whole place is on fire — but even if it’s not some big dramatic upset, if I’m just off or wound up, yeah, it can hit me that way.
Do you feel a lot of distress or emotional discomfort specifically about these episodes of eating, like they’re really bothering you or taking up a lot of your thoughts?

Yeah… afterward, definitely. That’s usually when it hits me.

I’ll be standing there with the wrappers or whatever, and I just feel… ashamed, I guess. Kind of disgusted with myself. Which sounds harsh, but that’s the word that comes up.

I’ve always thought of myself as a pretty disciplined guy, you know? I show up to work, do what I’m supposed to do, people can count on me. My dad was big on that kind of thing too — if you say you’re going to do something, you do it. So when I’m sneaking food or eating like that when nobody’s around, it feels like I’m being some other version of myself. Like I’m letting myself down.

I don’t know if I sit and think about it all day, but it bothers me. More than I’d like to admit.

Stress probably makes it worse. Work’s been a mess with the line changes — they move one thing and suddenly everybody’s acting like the whole place is on fire — but even if it’s not some big dramatic upset, if I’m just off or wound up, yeah, it can hit me that way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences marked distress regarding the eating episodes, which is a key criterion for Binge Eating Disorder (F50.8) as opposed to Eating Disorder, Unspecified (F50.2).
doctor.question: Do you feel a lot of distress or emotional discomfort specifically about these episodes of eating, like they’re really bothering you or taking up a lot of your thoughts?

target_item.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
target_item.manifestation: Afterward I feel ashamed and kind of disgusted with myself, because I’ve always thought of myself as disciplined and dependable, and this makes me feel like I’m sneaking around and letting myself down.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about emotional distress and discomfort related to the binge-eating episodes, which best matches feeling ashamed, disgusted, or guilty afterward.

patient.answer:
Yeah… afterward, definitely. That’s usually when it hits me.

I’ll be standing there with the wrappers or whatever, and I just feel… ashamed, I guess. Kind of disgusted with myself. Which sounds harsh, but that’s the word that comes up.

I’ve always thought of myself as a pretty disciplined guy, you know? I show up to work, do what I’m supposed to do, people can count on me. My dad was big on that kind of thing too — if you say you’re going to do something, you do it. So when I’m sneaking food or eating like that when nobody’s around, it feels like I’m being some other version of myself. Like I’m letting myself down.

I don’t know if I sit and think about it all day, but it bothers me. More than I’d like to admit.

There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors to suggest Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2 is more accurate than F50.8 in this context).
